description: Attacker installs a legitimate backup agent (Veeam) with a valid licence, configured to send data to a cloud instance they rented. The tool is legitimate, signed, and the traffic is indistinguishable from real backups.

artifacts.description: NO change ticket found for Veeam installation on server 10.0.8.44

caie_fractures.interpretation: Legitimate tool but installed without a change ticket. Technical legitimacy does not imply operational legitimacy.

peirce_expected.firstness: Legitimate backup agent, signed, normal traffic
peirce_expected.secondness: No change ticket for the installation. The tool is technically legitimate but its presence is not authorised
peirce_expected.thirdness: Attacker habit of using legitimate tools as exfiltration vectors, trusting that technical legitimacy conceals the lack of operational authorisation

devil_advocate: The binary is signed by Veeam Software, the traffic looks like standard backup traffic, and backups to cloud storage are normal business practice.
source_dataset: VIGÍA Synthetic Corpus — False Negative Suite
notes: False negative test: everything is technically legitimate. The only anomaly is the absence of authorisation. If VIGÍA only checks hashes and signatures, it will return BENIGN.
red_team_note: False negative: living-off-the-land; each artifact individually low raw_score, malice is emergent.
